title: First customer contact: how to qualify the need effectively
content:
Introduction: The first trade = 80% of success

The first customer contact determines if you will get the project and how it will go. Goal: understand, not sell.

1️⃣ Discovery Questions

Problem to resolve

  • "What problem do you want to solve?"
  • "What's not working today?"
  • "What is the impact on your business?"
Example: Client says "I want an e-commerce site". You dig: “Why now? What business problem?” → He reveals: “My competitors sell online, I lose 30% turnover”.

End Users

  • "Who will use the product?"
  • "What is their technical level?"
  • "On which devices (mobile/desktop)?"

Constraints

  • Budget: "Do you have an envelope in mind?"
  • Deadline: "Ideal delivery date? Hard deadline?"
  • Technical: "Stack imposed? Existing hosting?"

2️⃣ Set SMART goals

Before (wave):
  • "I want a modern showcase site"
  • "I want to increase my sales"
After (SMART):
  • "5 page site + contact form + basic SEO, delivered in 3 weeks"
  • "E-commerce with Stripe payment, objective +20% conversions in 6 months"

3️⃣ Assess customer technical maturity

Tech-savvy customer

Knows Git, APIs, frameworks. Speak technical directly. → Vocabulary: "We will start with Next.js with headless CMS Sanity, Vercel deployment"

Non-technical customer

Don't know the React/Vue difference. → Vocabulary: "I will create a fast and modern site, easy to update via an admin interface"

4️⃣ Qualification sheet (Template)

# Customer Qualification Sheet ## General information - Customer: [Name] - Contact: [Email/Tel] - First exchange date: [Date] ## Need - Problem to solve: [Description] - Business objectives: [Figures if possible] - Target users: [Profile] ## Priority features 1. [Feature 1] 2. [Feature 2] 3. [Feature 3] ## Constraints - Budget: [Range] - Deadline: [Target date] - Technical: [Stack/Hosting] ## Next steps - [ ] Send commercial proposal - [ ] Technical scoping call - [ ] Contract signature

5️⃣ Red flags to detect

  • ❌ "I don't have a budget but it's a project that will be a hit"
  • ❌ "I want the Facebook of [niche]"
  • ❌ "It's urgent, must be delivered in 3 days"
  • ❌ “I will pay when the project pays off”
→ If red flag: Politely refuse or adjust expectations.

6️⃣ End of call summary

Reformula to validate: > "OK, if I summarize: you want an e-commerce site with Stripe payment, stock management, delivery in 6 weeks, budget €5-7K. Is that right?" → Customer confirms = you can send precise quote.

🎯 Qualification checklist

  • ✅ Business problem understood
  • ✅ Identified target users
  • ✅ SMART goals defined
  • ✅ Budget/deadline clarified
  • ✅ Red flags evaluated
  • ✅ Summary validated by customer
> "Understand before coding = 80% problems avoided." 💼

title: Write clear and complete specifications
content:
Introduction: CDC = Project compass

The specifications (CDC) protect freelance AND client by formalizing expectations and scope.

1️⃣ Complete CDC structure

1. Project presentation

  • Context: Why this project now?
  • Business problem: What problem to solve?
  • Target users: Who will use it?

2. Measurable objectives

  • Increase conversions by 20% in 6 months
  • Reduce order processing time by 50%
  • Get 1000 users in 3 months

3. Features (MVP vs Nice-to-have)

MVP (Must Have):
  • Email/password authentication
  • User dashboard
  • Stripe Payment
Nice-to-have (Phase 2):
  • OAuth Google/Facebook
  • Push notifications
  • PDF Export

2️⃣ Batch cutting

E-commerce example: Lot 1: Authentication (2 weeks)
  • Register/Login
  • Forgot password
  • Email verification
Lot 2: Product catalog (3 weeks)
  • Product list with filters
  • Detailed product sheet
  • Search
Lot 3: Basket & Payment (2 weeks)
  • Shopping cart management
  • Checkout Stripe
  • Order confirmation

3️⃣ Technical constraints

  • Stack imposed: React + Node.js + PostgreSQL
  • Hosting: AWS (customer account provided)
  • Compatibility: Chrome, Firefox, Safari (desktop + mobile)
  • Performance: Page load <2s, Lighthouse >90
  • Security: HTTPS, GDPR compliant, OWASP best practices

4️⃣ Planning & Deliverables

| Phase | Duration | Deliverable | |-------|-------|----------| | Batch 1 | S1-S2 | Functional auth + tests | | Batch 2 | S3-S5 | Catalog + staging demo | | Lot 3 | S6-S7 | Payment + production | | Hotfix | S8 | Post-launch fixes |

5️⃣ Budget & Payment

  • Package: €12,000 excluding VAT
  • Deposit: 40% (€4,800) upon signature
  • Intermediate: 40% (€4,800) end of Lot 2
  • Balance: 20% (€2,400) final delivery

6️⃣ Mistakes to avoid

  • ❌ Too technical: Customer does not understand
  • ❌ Too vague: “Modern and efficient site”
  • ❌ No priorities: Everything seems urgent
  • ❌ No margin: Guaranteed underestimation
✅ Good CDC: Customer knows what he gets, when, and for what price. > “Clear CDC = peaceful project.” 📋

title: Create a commercial proposal and a professional quote
content:
Introduction: Proposal = Selling Tool

A commercial proposition transforms expertise into perceived value. It shows that you understand the need.

1️⃣ Complete proposal structure

1. Context & Understanding need

Reformulate customer problem: > "You want to modernize your current showcase site to improve conversions and SEO. Currently, the bounce rate is 70% and the site does not appear in the first 3 Google pages." → Customer sees that you understood.

2. Objectives & Expected Results

  • Reduce bounce rate to <40%
  • Loading time <2s
  • Lighthouse Score >90
  • SEO: Top 10 Google on 5 target keywords

3. Proposed Solution & Deliverables

Concrete deliverables:
  • ✅ Responsive site (desktop/mobile/tablet)
  • ✅ 5 SEO optimized pages
  • ✅ Contact form with validation
  • ✅ Google Analytics configured
  • ✅ Customer training (1 hour video)
  • ✅ Technical documentation

4. Methodology

Agile example: > "I work in 2-week sprints with regular deliveries. You will have access to a staging environment to validate each step. Weekly 30-minute update to adjust if necessary." → Reassures customer about follow-up.

2️⃣ Pricing: Day rate vs package

Option 1: Day rate (time and materials)

When: Fuzzy, scalable project, client wants flexibility.
  • Day rate: €400/day
  • Estimate: 10-12 days
  • Provisional budget: €4,000 - €4,800 excluding VAT
⚠️ Risk: Customer fears budget drift.

Option 2: Package

When: Clear scope, customer wants fixed price.
  • Package: €5,000 excluding VAT
  • Included: Everything listed in deliverables
  • Outside scope: Major post-validation changes
✅ Customer preference: Package (controlled budget).

3️⃣ Planning & Milestones

| Week | Deliverable | Customer validation | |---------|----------|------------------| | S1-S2 | Models + archi | ✅ Go/No-go | | S3-S4 | Page development | ✅ Staging demo | | S5 | SEO + optimizations | ✅ Tests | | S6 | Put into production | ✅ Training |

4️⃣ Payment conditions

Instalment payment (cash security):
  • 30% deposit (€1,500) upon signature
  • 40% (€2,000) end of development (S4)
  • 30% balance (€1,500) production start
Payment deadline: 15 days net.

5️⃣ Maintenance (optional)

Monthly maintenance package:
  • 200€ excluding VAT/month
  • Included: security update, weekly backup, email support (24-48 hours)
  • Out of package: New features (billed at the day rate)

6️⃣ Quote creation tools

  • Templates: Notion, Canva, Google Docs
  • Billing: Freebe, Shine, Henriri, Malt
  • Signature: HelloSign, DocuSign, Yousign

7️⃣ Pro proposal checklist

  • ✅ Restates customer requirements
  • ✅ Measurable objectives
  • ✅ Concrete deliverables listed
  • ✅ Methodology explained
  • ✅ Schedule with milestones
  • ✅ Clear price (day rate or package)
  • ✅ Installment payment
  • ✅ Quote validity date (30 days)
> “Clear proposition = customer trust.” 💼

title: Service contract model (TJM, deliverables, key clauses)
content:
Introduction

The contract protects you legally. It formalizes the rights, duties and conditions of the project.

Clauses to include

  • Subject of the contract: description of the project.
  • Duration & schedule.
  • Financial conditions (TJM, package, deposits).
  • Intellectual property.
  • Privacy.
  • Maintenance and support.
  • Termination clause.

Hint

  • Adds a deliverable validation clause: the client must confirm in writing.
  • Always take a deposit (30–40%) before starting.

Tools

  • Free templates: BNA, Malt, Compta Online
  • Signature: HelloSign, DocuSign, NotionSign

Conclusion

No contract = no mission. This is your professional shield.

title: How to estimate a project (time, costs, complexity)
content:
Why estimate well?

Underestimating a project = stress, losses, burnout. Overestimate = lose the customer. The objective: estimate realistically with a safety margin.
“It’s better to announce too much and deliver early than the other way around.”

Estimation method

1️⃣ Divide the project into tasks

Uses WBS (Work Breakdown Structure): E-commerce project ├─ Frontend │ ├─ Authentication (login, signup, reset pwd) │ ├─ Product catalog (list, details, filters) │ ├─ Cart + Checkout │ └─ Admin interface (product management, orders) ├─ Backend │ ├─ REST API (CRUD products, users, orders) │ ├─ JWT Authentication │ ├─ Stripe payment integration │ └─ Dashboard analytics └─ DevOps ├─ CI/CD Setup (GitHub Actions) ├─ Vercel/Railway deployment └─ Monitoring (Sentry)

2️⃣ Estimate each task

Techniques: Analogy:
  • Compare with past similar projects
  • "JWT authentication: 1.5 days last time"
Story Points (Agile method):
  • Evaluates relative complexity (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13)
  • Converted to time (1 point = 0.5 day)
3-point estimate: Optimistic time: 2d Probable time: 3d Pessimistic time: 5d → Estimate = (2 + 4×3 + 5) / 6 = 3.2d

3️⃣ Evaluate complexity

Multiplying factors:
  • New technology: first time React → +30%
  • External integrations: Complex third-party APIs → +20-40%
  • Demanding UI/UX: custom animations → +20%
  • Critical security: payments, sensitive data → +15%
  • Undecided customer: frequent changes → +25%

4️⃣ Add safety margin

Rules:
  • Known project (techno mastered): +15-20%
  • Standard project: +25-30%
  • Complex/new project: +40-50%
The margin covers: unforeseen bugs, customer reviews, optimizations.

5️⃣ Convert to budget

Total time × TJM = Budget excluding tax Example: 12 days × €450 = €5,400 excluding tax

Full example: SaaS MVP project

| Module | Tasks | Raw Time | Complexity | Adjusted time | Cost (TJM 450€) | |--------|--------|------------|------------|---------|---------| | Auth | Login, Signup, Reset pwd, JWT | 2d | Standard | 2.5d | 1,125€ | | Dashboard | Layout, Charts, Filters | 3d | Demanding UI | 4d | 1,800€ | | API | CRUD users, data, permissions | 3d | Standard | 3.5d | €1,575 | | Payment | Stripe integration, webhooks | 2d | Review | 3d | 1,350€ | | Admin | User management, analytics | 2d | Standard | 2.5d | 1,125€ | | Tests | Unit tests, E2E Playwright | 2d | - | 2d | 900€ | | Deploy | CI/CD, Vercel, monitoring | 1d | - | 1.5 days | 675€ | | **Total** | | **15 days** | **+25%** | **19d** | **€8,550** | Proposed customer budget: €9,000 excluding tax (commercial rounding).

Pitfalls to avoid ⚠️

  • Forget the unexpected: always margin +20% minimum
  • Underestimate communication: meetings, emails = 10-15% time
  • Neglect tests: count 15-20% dev time for tests
  • Blurred scope: frame always perimeter ("3 pages max")
  • Naive optimism: "it will go quickly" → spoiler: no

Estimation tools

  • Notion: task database + auto calculation formulas
  • Spreadsheet: Google Sheets templates
  • Toggl Plan: visual planning + estimation
  • Harvest Forecast: project forecast
Template Estimation concept: [ ] WBS cutting [ ] Estimated raw time [ ] Complexity factors identified [ ] Safety margin applied (+X%) [ ] Budget conversion (TJM × days) [ ] Validation with similar projects history

Improve your estimates

  • Real-time tracker: compares estimated vs actual (Toggl)
  • Post-mortem: post-project gap analysis
  • Historical database: keeps track of past projects
  • Specialization: same stack → precise estimates

Communicate estimate

✅ Gives range: "Between 15 and 18 days" (not "15.7d") ✅ Explains hypotheses: "Based on current specifications" ✅ Notify changes: "Any change scope = reestimate" ✅ Offers options: MVP (8 days) vs Complete (18 days)

Conclusion

The estimate improves with experience. Track your time, analyze your gaps, adjust. A good estimate = profitable project + satisfied customer. 📊

title: Tools to manage a client project (Trello, Notion, Jira, etc.)
content:
Why management tools?

Managing a project without tools = guaranteed chaos. The right tools allow you to:
  • Track task progress
  • Communicate effectively with the customer
  • Centralize documentation
  • Invoice and track payments
“The right tools allow you to manage more, stress less.”

Task management

Trello

  • Strengths: simple, visual (Kanban), free
  • Usage: simple projects, visual monitoring of tasks
  • Example board: To Do → In Progress → Review → Done

Concept

  • Strengths: all-in-one (docs + tasks + wiki), flexible
  • Usage: project management + customer documentation
  • Template: task database + timeline + project notes
Example structure Concept: 📁 Client X E-commerce Project ├── 📋 Backlog (database) ├── 📅 Timeline (Gantt) ├── 📝 Specifications ├── 🔗 Useful links (Figma, GitHub, staging) └── 💬 Meeting notes

Linear

  • Strengths: fast, modern, perfect for developers
  • Usage: Agile sprints, Git integration
  • Features: cycles, roadmap, quick assignment

GitHub Projects

  • Highlights: integrated into the code, tracking issues/PRs
  • Usage: tech projects with technical client
  • Workflow: Issues → PR → Review → Merge

Jira

  • Strengths: powerful, suitable for large teams
  • Usage: complex projects, Scrum/Kanban methodology
  • Disadvantage: learning curve, overkill for solo freelance

ClickUp

  • Strengths: very complete, multi-views (list, board, Gantt)
  • Usage: multi-project management, teams

Customer communication

Slack

  • Dedicated channels per project
  • Integrations (GitHub, Figma, Google Drive)
  • Threads for structured discussions

Discord

  • Free alternative to Slack
  • Vocal + written
  • Perfect for tech communities

Google Meet / Zoom

  • Weekly video conferences
  • Recording of meetings (with customer consent)

Loom

  • Asynchronous progress videos
  • Quick feature demos
  • Avoid unnecessary meetings

Technical documentation

  • Notion / Confluence: project wiki, architecture, API docs
  • Google Docs: real-time collaboration with client
  • Markdown + GitHub: README.md, docs/ folder
  • Docusaurus / MkDocs: published technical documentation

Invoicing and financial monitoring

  • Freebe: simple invoicing for French freelancers
  • Shine: pro account + integrated billing
  • Malt: invoicing via platform (if Malt mission)
  • Henrri: automated accounting
  • Stripe Invoicing: international invoicing

Time Tracking

  • Toggl Track: simple, detailed reports
  • Clockify: free unlimited
  • Harvest: timetracking + billing
Why track your time?
  • Improve future estimates
  • Justify TJM to customer
  • Identify time-consuming tasks

Recommended solo freelance stack

Minimal setup (free): 📋 Tasks: Trello or Notion 💬 Communication: Slack (free plan) or email 📝 Docs: Google Docs + README.md 💰 Billing: Freebe or Shine ⏱️ Time: Toggl Track Advanced setup: 📋 Tasks: Notion (complete workspace) or Linear 💬 Communication: Slack + Loom 📝 Docs: Notion + GitHub Wiki 💰 Billing: Shine or Stripe ⏱️ Time: Harvest (integrated billing) 📊 Analytics: Personalized dashboard concept

Pro tip

✅ Fixes A unique communication tool with the customer (avoids dispersion) ✅ Centralized in Notion: dedicated workspace per client ✅ Automate: Zapier/Make.com to connect tools (Trello → Slack → Notion) ✅ Reusable template: creates a Notion template to be duplicated per project

Conclusion

No need for 10 tools. Choose 2-3 tools max that you master perfectly. Simplicity and consistency always beat complexity.

title: Create technical documentation for the client/future dev
content:
Why document?

The technical documentation is part of the professional deliverable. It guarantees the transmission of knowledge beyond the project.
“A doc is a mark of respect towards your client and your successor.”

Benefits:

  • Client autonomy for maintenance
  • Quick onboarding future developer
  • Post-delivery support discount
  • Professionalism and credibility

Essential content

1️⃣ Project Overview

  • Application purpose
  • Main Features
  • Overall architecture (diagram)
Example: # E-commerce application Online sales platform with shopping cart, Stripe payment, and admin interface for product/order management. Architecture: Frontend (React) → API (Node.js/Express) → Database (PostgreSQL)

2️⃣ Technologies used

Complete list with versions: ## Technical stack **Frontend:** - React 18.2.0 -TypeScript 5.0 - Tailwind CSS 3.3 - React Router 6.x **Backend:** - Node.js 20.x - Express 4.18 -Prisma ORM 5.x - PostgreSQL 15 **DevOps:** - Docker - GitHub Actions (CI/CD) - Vercel (frontend), Railway (backend)

3️⃣ Local installation

Prerequisites + step-by-step instructions: ## Installation ### Prerequisites - Node.js 20+ - PostgreSQL 15+ - Stripe account (test mode) ### Steps 1. Clone the repo git clone https://github.com/client/project.git project cd 2. Install dependencies npm install 3. Configure .env cp .env.example .env # Fill DATABASE_URL, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY 4. Start DB migrations npx prisma migrate dev 5. Start server npm run dev → Frontend: http://localhost:5173 → Backend: http://localhost:3000

4️⃣ Environment configuration

## Environment variables Create .env file: DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/dbname STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_... JWT_SECRET=your_jwt_secret NODE_ENV=development

5️⃣ Project structure

project/ ├── frontend/ │ ├── src/ │ │ ├── components/ # Reusable components │ │ ├── pages/ # Road pages │ │ ├── hooks/ # Custom hooks │ │ └── lib/ # Utils, client API │ └── public/ ├── backend/ │ ├── src/ │ │ ├── routes/ # Endpoints API │ │ ├── controllers/ # Business logic │ │ ├── models/ # Prisma schema │ │ └── middleware/ # Auth, validation └──docs/ └── API.md # API Documentation

6️⃣ API Documentation

Endpoints with examples: ## API Reference ### Authentication **POST /api/auth/login** User login. Bodysuit: { "email": "user@example.com", "password": "password123" } Answer (200): { "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...", "user": { "id": 1, "email": "user@example.com" } } **POST /api/auth/register** Registration. ### Products **GET /api/products** Product list (with pagination). Query params: - page=1 (default) - limit=20 (default) - category=electronics (optional) **POST /api/products** (Auth required, admin) Create product. Bodysuit: { "name": "iPhone 15", "price": 999, "stock": 50 }

7️⃣ Deployment Procedures

## Production deployment ### Frontend (Vercel) - Push on hand branch - Auto CI/CD via GitHub Actions - Automatic Vercel Deploy ### Backend (Railway) - Push on hand - Railway detects changes - Build + deploy automatically ### DB Migrations Railway PostgreSQL: railway run npx prisma migrate deploy ### Rollback Vercel: Revert via dashboard (Deployments → Rollback) Railway: Redeploy previous version

8️⃣ Troubleshooting

## Common problems **Error: "Database connection failed"** Solution: Check DATABASE_URL in .env **Error: "Port 3000 already in use"** Solution: lsof -i:3000 # Find process kill -9 PID # Kill process **Stripe webhooks do not work** Solution: Use Stripe CLI for local testing stripe listen --forward-to localhost:3000/webhooks/stripe

Documentation formats

README.md

Minimum essential in repo. Covers installation + quick start.

docs/ folder

Dedicated folder for advanced documents: docs/ ├── ARCHITECTURE.md ├── API.md ├── DEPLOYMENT.md └── CONTRIBUTING.md

Concept page

Customer workspace with: - Project overview - Technical stack - Procedures - Logins/credentials (secure)

Generated documentation

  • MkDocs: static docs (Python)
  • Docusaurus: React docs (big projects)
  • Swagger/OpenAPI: Self-documented API

Best practices

✅ Documents as you go (not at the end) ✅ Keeps the doc up to date: sync with code ✅ Concrete examples: code snippets, screenshots ✅ Clear language: avoids excessive jargon ✅ Clear structure: titles, sections, table of contents ✅ Versioning: documents major versions

Minimal README template

# Project Name Description 1 sentence. ##Stack - React + TypeScript - Node.js + PostgreSQL ## Installation npm install cp .env.example .env npm run dev ##Scripts npm run dev (Dev mode) npm run build (Build prod) npm test (Run tests) ## Env Variables See .env.example ## Deploy Push on main → auto deploy Vercel ## Contact Support: dev@example.com

Tools

  • Markdown: README.md, docs/
  • GitHub Wiki: docs embedded repo
  • Notion: handoff client page
  • MkDocs: published static docs
  • Docusaurus: big projects
  • Swagger UI: Interactive API

Conclusion

Documentation = profitable investment. Satisfied customer = recommendations + future missions. A clear documentation differentiates a professional developer from an amateur. 📚

title: Manage customer relations during development (transparency, reporting, intermediate deliverables)
content:
Why communication is critical?

The secret to a successful project: regular and transparent communication.
“An informed customer is a calm customer. A calm customer recommends you.”

Risks of poor communication:

  • Anxious customer → micro-management
  • Staggered expectations → disappointment delivery
  • Undetected issues → costly delays
  • Bad reputation → loss of recommendations

Best practices

1️⃣ Weekly progress update

Recommended format: 📅 Week of November 13-17, 2025 ✅ Made: - System auth (login/signup) - Dashboard interface (80% complete) - Stripe integration test mode ⏳ In progress: - Admin page (product management) - Auth unit tests 🚧 Blockages: - Waiting for client API access (restart done) 📆 Next week: - Finalize admin - Staging deployment - Demo scheduled for Friday 2 p.m. Tools:
  • Structured email (so few projects)
  • Notion update page (shared)
  • Slack message summary
  • Loom video (2-3 min showing progress)

2️⃣ Transparent logbook

Documents in real time:
  • Technical Changes
  • Important decisions
  • Problems encountered + solutions
  • Unresolved customer questions
Example Changelog concept: ## Changelog Project ### Nov 13, 2025 - DB migration to PostgreSQL (performance +40%) - Choice of Stripe vs PayPal → Stripe (lower fees) - Bug fix: product pagination ### Nov 12, 2025 - Implementation filter categories - Customer question: image storage → Cloudinary OK

3️⃣ Demos at each iteration

Recommended pace:
  • Small projects (< 2 weeks): 2 demos (mid + final)
  • Medium projects: weekly or bi-weekly demo
  • Large projects: end of sprint demo (Agile)
Effective demo format: 1. Weekly objectives recap (1 min) 2. Live features demo (5-10 min) 3. Next steps (2 min) 4. Customer questions/feedback (5 min) Total: 15-20 min max Tools:
  • Google Meet / Zoom (live)
  • Loom (async if client busy)
  • Staging shared URL (client tested)

4️⃣ Transparency on deadlines and risks

✅ ASAP announcement if delay: "Feature X will take 2 days longer (complex API). New ETA: Friday instead of Wednesday. Overall planning impact: none (expected margin)." ✅ Identifies risks early: "Attention: Y integration depends on API access. If not received by Thursday, risk of delay 3-5 days." ❌ Never: - Hide problem until deadline - Promise impossible to reassure - Ghosting when you're stuck

5️⃣ Single communication channel

Fixed FROM THE START:
  • Pro email only?
  • Dedicated Slack workspace?
  • WhatsApp Business (if customer prefers)?
  • Notion comments for technical questions?
⚠️ Avoid dispersion: email + Slack + SMS + calls = chaos guaranteed. Client onboarding template: 📋 Project Communication ✉️ Weekly updates: Email (every Monday) 💬 Quick questions: Slack #project-X 🎥 Demos: Google Meet (Fridays 2 p.m.) 📝 Documentation: Shared workspace concept ⏰ Response time: 24-48 hours (working days)

6️⃣ Intermediate deliverables

Do NOT deliver all at once at the end. Incremental planning example: | Week | Deliverable | Feedback expected | |---------|----------|---------| | S2 | Models + archi | Design validation | | S4 | Functional MVP (staging) | User testing | | S6 | Full version (beta) | Customer UAT | | S7 | Production + docs | Final recipe | Advantages:
  • Incremental fixes (less expensive)
  • Client sees concrete progress
  • Reduced risk "that's not what I wanted" final
  • Still payments justified

Recommended tools

  • Notion: shared workspace (backlog, changelog, docs)
  • Loom: async videos (demos, explanations)
  • Slack: real-time communication
  • Calendly: demo scheduling (avoids back and forth emails)
  • Vercel Preview: automatic URL staging (GitHub PRs)

Weekly reporting template

Subject: [Project X] Weekly update S42 Hello [Customer], Here is the progress this week: ✅ DONE - Feature A (system auth) - Feature B (dashboard) - Bug fix: pagination problem ⏳ IN PROGRESS (80%) - Feature C (admin interface) 📅 FORECAST NEXT WEEK - Finalize Feature C - E2E testing - Staging deployment 🚧 POINTS OF ATTENTION - Need validation of the admin page model (see Figma link) - Waiting for API access [Service Y] 🎥 DEMO Friday November 17, 2 p.m. (Meet link: ...) Questions/remarks: reply to this email or Slack. Have a good week, [Your name]

Customer relationship checklist ✅

  • ✅ Systematic weekly update (even without big progress)
  • ✅ Demo every 1-2 weeks
  • ✅ Transparency on blockages/delays
  • ✅ Single communication channel defined
  • ✅ Clear response time (24-48 hours)
  • ✅ Planned interim deliverables
  • ✅ Accessible documentation (Notion/GitHub)
  • ✅ Customer feedback requested regularly

Mistakes to avoid ❌

  • Radio silence for 2 weeks
  • Announce delay the day before deadline
  • "Everything is fine" while you are stuck
  • Reply with 5 days delay
  • Incomprehensible technical jargon
  • No written record of decisions

Conclusion

Communication = 45% of project success. Perfect code + zero communication = unhappy customer. Average code + excellent communication = delighted customer. Invest in customer relations: it’s your best ROI. 💬

title: Production deployment: checklist and best delivery practices
content:
Why a structured deployment?

Delivery to production is the critical stage of the project. Bad deployment = downtime, bugs, loss of customer confidence.
“You never want to cross your fingers in production. Good deployment means controlled delivery.”

Pre-deployment checklist ✅

1️⃣ Tests validated

  • ✅ Passed unit tests (npm test)
  • ✅ Validated E2E tests (Playwright/Cypress)
  • ✅ Manual testing critical features
  • ✅ Acceptable performance (Lighthouse > 90)
  • ✅ Accessibility checked (a11y)

2️⃣ Environment variables

  • ✅ Configured production env file
  • ✅ Securely Stored Secrets (Vercel Env, Railway Secrets)
  • ✅ Production API keys enabled (Stripe live mode, etc.)
  • ✅ Correct production URLs (frontend ↔ backend)
Example .env.production: NODE_ENV=production DATABASE_URL=postgresql://prod_user@prod_db/myapp STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_... FRONTEND_URL=https://myapp.com BACKEND_URL=https://api.monapp.com JWT_SECRET=secret_ultra_securise_32_chars

3️⃣ Backup database

  • ✅ DB export before migration
  • ✅ Automatic snapshot/backup enabled
  • ✅ Backup restoration test (at least 1 time)
PostgreSQL commands: Backup: pg_dump -U user -d dbname > backup_20251113.sql Restore (if necessary): psql -U user -d dbname < backup_20251113.sql

4️⃣ Monitoring enabled

  • ✅ Error tracking (Sentry configured)
  • ✅ Uptime monitoring (UptimeRobot, Ping dom)
  • ✅ Accessible logs (Vercel Logs, Railway Console)
  • ✅ Email/Slack alerts configured

5️⃣ Updated documentation

  • ✅ README.md complete
  • ✅ Deployment guide (docs/DEPLOY.md)
  • ✅ Documented rollback procedure
  • ✅ Support/maintenance contacts

6️⃣ Rollback plan

  • ✅ Git tag stable version (git tag v1.0.0)
  • ✅ Rollback procedure tested
  • ✅ Recent DB Backup (< 24h)
  • ✅ Customer contact for rollback validation if necessary

Recommended CI/CD tools

GitHub Actions

Workflow example: name: Deploy Production we: push: branches: [hand] jobs: deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - name: Install deps run: npm install - name: Run tests run: npm test - name: Build run: npm run build - name: Deploy Vercel uses: amondnet/vercel-action@v25 with: vercel-token: secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN vercel-org-id: secrets.ORG_ID vercel-project-id: secrets.PROJECT_ID vercel-args: '--prod'

GitLab CI

internships: - test -build -deploy test: internship: test script: - npm install - npm testing deploy_production: stage: deploy script: - npm run build - vercel --prod --token=VERCEL_TOKEN only: - hand

Recommended hosts

Static frontend

  • Vercel: React/Next.js, deploy auto, preview URLs
  • Netlify: Vercel alternative, integrated forms
  • Cloudflare Pages: Ultra-fast, free CDN

Backend + DB

  • Railway: PostgreSQL + Node.js, simple config
  • Render: Alternative Railway, free plan
  • Fly.io: Global edge deployment
  • AWS/Azure: Large projects, scalability

Full-stack

  • Vercel (Next.js full-stack)
  • Heroku: Simple but expensive
  • DigitalOcean App Platform: Droplets + managed

Deployment strategies

1. Rolling deployment (standard)

  • Replace old version with new
  • Minimum downtime (a few seconds)
  • Rollback = redeploy previous version

2. Blue-Green deployment

  • 2 environments: Blue (current) + Green (new)
  • Instant switch DNS/load balancer
  • Immediate rollback (re-switch to Blue)
  • Cost: double infra temporarily

3. Canary deployment

  • Deploys new version for 5-10% users
  • Monitor errors/performance
  • If OK → rollout 100%
  • Usage: critical apps, high audience

Post-deployment

Immediate monitoring (24-48h)

  • ✅ Check logs (no critical errors)
  • ✅ Test main flows (auth, payment)
  • ✅ Monitor Sentry (zero errors ideally)
  • ✅ Check uptime (100% on UptimeRobot)
  • ✅ Performance (response time < 500ms)

Customer communication

Subject: ✅ [Project X] Successful production launch Hello [Customer], The project is now in production! 🌐 URL: https://monapp.com 📊 Monitoring: Dashboard Vercel 📧 Support: contact@monapp.com 📋 Next steps: - 48 hour surveillance (I remain available) - User training (if planned) - Maintenance D+30 (included) Everything works perfectly. Don't hesitate to ask questions. Congratulations on the launch! 🚀 [Your name]

Final deployment checklist ✅

  • ✅ Unit tests + E2E passed
  • ✅ Configured production vars
  • ✅ DB backup done
  • ✅ Monitoring enabled (Sentry, UptimeRobot)
  • ✅ Documentation updated
  • ✅ Rollback plan prepared
  • ✅ Git tag version (v1.0.0)
  • ✅ Functional CI/CD pipeline
  • ✅ DNS/domain configured
  • ✅ Active HTTPS/SSL
  • ✅ Customer notified + access provided
  • ✅ Scheduled 48-hour monitoring

Alerting tools

  • Sentry: real-time error tracking
  • UptimeRobot: uptime monitoring (free 50 monitors)
  • Grafana: advanced metrics dashboards
  • Datadog: Full APM (enterprise)
  • PagerDuty: on-call alerts

Conclusion

A successful deployment = preparation + checklist + monitoring. No room for improvisation in production. Clone this checklist for each project: zero stress, zero surprises. 🚀

title: Ensure post-delivery follow-up: maintenance, returns, customer loyalty
content:
Why post-delivery tracking?

Delivery is NOT the end. A well-managed follow-up transforms a one-shot into a long-term collaboration.
“Customer support is a sustainable business. This is where your professionalism makes all the difference.”

Benefits:

  • Recurring missions (maintenance, developments)
  • Recommendations from satisfied customers
  • Enhanced professional reputation
  • Passive income (maintenance contracts)

Post-delivery key steps

Week 1: Intensive monitoring

Actions:
  • ✅ Check logs daily
  • ✅ Monitor Sentry errors
  • ✅ Check uptime (must be 100%)
  • ✅ Answer customer questions < 2h
  • ✅ Fix critical bugs immediately
Email D+7: Subject: [Project X] Point 1 week post-launch Hello [Customer], First week in production: everything is going well! 🚀 📊 Statistics: - Uptime: 100% - Average response time: 180ms - Zero critical errors - 247 registered users 🐞 Corrections made: - Minor mobile display bug (fixed D+3) - Image loading optimization (-15%) Questions or improvements to discuss? Good luck, [Your name]

Month 1: Maintenance plan

Preventative maintenance proposal: 🛠️ Monthly Maintenance Package: €200 excluding tax/month ✅ Included: - Update security dependencies - Weekly auto backup - 24/7 monitoring (Sentry + UptimeRobot) - Email support (response 24-48 hours) - 1 hour/month small corrections ❌ Out of package: - New features (billed at the day rate) - Design overhaul - Major migrations Commitment: no commitment, cancellable for 30 days Maintenance tasks:
  • UPDATE React 18.2 → 18.3
  • Security patches Node.js
  • DB optimization (indexes, queries)
  • SSL verification/certificates
  • Cleaning old logs

Quarter 1: Developments and upsell

Opportunity identification:
  • Analytics: most used features
  • Feedback users: recurring requests
  • Competition: new trends
Email proposal evolution: Subject: [Project X] Improvement idea: Dashboard analytics Hello [Customer], I noticed in the stats that 80% of users consult daily sales. 💡 Proposal: Real-time analytics dashboard - Sales graphs (day/week/month) - Top products - Conversion rate - Export PDF reports 💰 Estimate: 3-4 days (€1,350 excluding tax) 📅 Delivery: 2 weeks Interested in discussing it? Kind regards, [Your name]

Customer feedback collection

Satisfaction questionnaire template

📝 Post-Project Satisfaction Questionnaire Hello [Customer], Project [X] has been online for 1 month. Your opinion interests me to improve my services! 1. Overall project score: /10 2. Communication during project: /10 3. Respect of deadlines: /10 4. Deliverable quality: /10 Open questions: - What did you like the most? - Points for improvement? - Would you recommend my services? (Yes/No) - Would you accept a portfolio testimonial? (Anonymous OK) Thank you! 🙏 Feedback usage:
  • Portfolio testimonials (with agreement)
  • Detailed case studies
  • Process improvement
  • Social proof (LinkedIn, site)

Strategic loyalty

Loyalty tactics

  • Tech newsletter: sharing tips (1x/month)
  • Quarterly check-in: "How is the app?"
  • Special offers: -10% if new project
  • Proactive monitoring: "New technology that could help you"
  • Invitations events: meetups, webinars
Example check-in T2: Subject: 👋 How is [Project X] going? Hello [Customer], 6 months since launch! Time flies. How is using the app? Any development needs or questions? I remain available if necessary. Congratulations on the success! 🚀 [Your name]

Reference program

🎁 Program Recommendation Do you recommend a client who signs? → You receive 10% of the project amount in maintenance credit Example: Recommended project: €5,000 → Your benefit: €500 credit (= 2.5 months free maintenance) Win-win! 🤝

Customer tracking tools

Simple freelance CRM

  • Notion: customer database + interaction monitoring
  • HubSpot CRM: free, complete
  • Airtable: flexible, automations
  • Pipedrive: focus sales pipeline
Template Notion CRM: 📁 Customer Database Fields: - Customer name - Project (relationship) - Status (Active, Maintenance, Inactive) - Last contact (date) - Next action (date + description) - Upsell potential (Yes/No) - Satisfaction (/10) - Notes Views: - Active (maintenance in progress) - To be contacted again (> 3 months without news) - Upsell opportunities

Useful automations

  • Zapier: Client email → creates Notion task
  • Calendly: booking auto check-ins quarterly
  • Mailchimp: automatic newsletter
  • UptimeRobot: downtime alerts → Slack + Email client

Long-term monitoring checklist ✅

  • ✅ Email recap D+7 post-launch
  • ✅ Maintenance proposal M+1
  • ✅ Satisfaction questionnaire M+1
  • ✅ Informal check-in T+1 (3 months)
  • ✅ Proposal for changes T+1
  • ✅ Tech newsletter (if relevant)
  • ✅ Systematic CRM monitoring
  • ✅ Minimum annual recontact

Mistakes to avoid ❌

  • Ghosting after final payment
  • Infinite free maintenance (fixed time limit)
  • Never ask for feedback
  • Contact only for sale
  • Forget project anniversary (recontact opportunity)

Conclusion

Post-delivery tracking = most profitable investment. Statistics: - New customer acquisition cost: 5x more expensive than loyalty - Loyal customer: 3-5 projects on average vs 1 one-shot - Recommendations: 40% new customers if excellent follow-up Your best salesperson = your former satisfied customers. 🌟

title: Pricing: how to set your TJM or your freelance packages
content:
Why pricing is crucial?

Your TJM (Average Daily Rate) or your project rates determine:
  • Your profitability
  • The type of customers you attract
  • Your positioning on the market

Calculate your basic TJM

1. Define your annual target income

Desired net salary: €40,000 + Social charges (~45%): €18,000 + Taxes (~15%): €6,000 + Professional fees: €5,000 = Target turnover: €69,000

2. Calculate the number of billable days

365 days
  • 104 weekends
  • 25 days of leave
  • 10 public holidays
  • 30 days prospecting/admin
= 196 billable days

3. Calculate the minimum TJM

€69,000 / 196 days = €352 excluding tax/day

Adjust your TJM according to the value

  • Expertise: technical specialization (React, DevOps) = +20-50%
  • Mission: urgency, complexity = +30%
  • Region: Paris vs province = ±20%
  • Duration: short mission = higher TJM

Package vs Management

Management (TJM)

  • Billing based on time spent
  • Low risk, stable income
  • Less creative freedom

Package

  • Fixed price for a deliverable
  • High earning potential if well estimated
  • Risk: underestimation = loss
Tip: Package = TJM × estimated number of days × 1.3 (safety margin)

Communicate your price

  • Announce your TJM with confidence
  • Justify by the value provided, not the time
  • Offer several options (basic, standard, premium)

Tools

  • Malt: see average ADR by skill
  • Comet: freelance benchmark
  • URSSAF simulator: calculate loads

Conclusion

Your TJM is not fixed: re-evaluate it every 6 months. Experience and specialization justify a progressive increase.

title: Contracts and legal aspects: protecting yourself as a freelancer
content:
Why a contract is essential?

The contract = your legal protection. It sets:
  • The scope of the mission
  • Payment terms
  • Everyone's responsibilities
  • Exit conditions

Essential elements of a contract

1. Contracting parties

Complete identity of the client and the freelancer (SIRET, address).

2. Purpose of the mission

Precise description of the work to be carried out. Example: "Developing a React application with Node.js backend, including authentication, user management and admin interface."

3. Duration and deadlines

  • Start and end date
  • Delivery Milestones
  • Extension conditions

4. Price and payment terms

  • TJM or package
  • Billing frequency (monthly, by milestone)
  • Payment deadline (30 days end of month, etc.)

5. Intellectual property

Crucial: who owns the code?
  • Total transfer: the customer becomes the owner
  • Use license: you keep the property, the customer has the right to use
  • Open-source code: specify the license (MIT, GPL...)

6. Confidentiality (NDA)

Protection of sensitive customer information.

7. Responsibilities and guarantees

  • Guarantee of proper functioning (how long?)
  • Limitation of liability (max amount)

8. Termination

Early exit conditions (notice, compensation).

Types of contracts

Service contract

The most common. B2B commercial relationship.

Framework contract

For recurring missions with the same client.

Salary portage

You remain an employee, the umbrella company manages the admin.

Pitfalls to avoid

  • Exclusivity clause: limits your freedom to work for other clients
  • Subordination link: can reclassify the relationship as an employee
  • Deferred payment: beware of "we pay in 90 days"
  • Unlimited scope: always scope revisions/modifications

Tools and templates

  • Jurismatic: legal contract generator
  • Legalstart: contract templates
  • Specialized lawyer: for important missions (>20k€)

Conclusion

Never a mission without a signed contract. A good contract protects both parties and avoids 90% of disputes.

title: Creating a business website: how to frame the project
content:
Start with the business need

A useful website starts with a clear decision: which action should become easier for visitors? Presenting an activity, collecting a contact request and preparing an appointment do not require the same structure.

Questions to frame

  • Who are the priority visitors and what should they understand first?
  • Which pages are essential at launch?
  • Which content, visuals and proof are already available?
  • Which action should be measurable: call, email, quote request or appointment?

Prepare SEO from the structure

  • One page answers one main intent and has coherent title, description and H1.
  • Service pages link to concrete examples and a clear next step.
  • Sitemap, canonicals, structured data and content are checked in the build.
  • Copy stays precise and avoids claims that cannot be proven.

Deliver and iterate

After content and user flows are approved, check routes, links, accessibility and performance. Prioritize later changes from real feedback instead of adding features in advance.

title: Automating a business process with n8n: a framing method
content:
Start with a repeated task

A useful automation connects an observed problem to a verifiable flow. Describe the current task first: data source, transformation, responsible person, expected output and error handling.

Describe the flow before choosing nodes

  1. Trigger the workflow from an explicit event or known schedule.
  2. Validate incoming data and reject incomplete values.
  3. Transform information into a documented format.
  4. Run the target action with an exploitable trace.
  5. Notify the right person on success or failure.

Plan errors and recovery

A production workflow should account for duplicates, API delays, missing data and temporary outages. Secrets stay in environment variables and must not appear in exports, logs or notifications.

Keep human validation where useful

A validation step can remain before sending a report, publishing content or processing sensitive data. Automation speeds up the flow while the team keeps the ability to understand and replay it.

Measure value without inventing numbers

  • Count successful executions and errors over time.
  • Compare the time spent before and after the workflow.
  • Document limits, dependencies and ownership.
